newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Montreal sees double-digit EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Bank Montreal sees double-digit EPS growth.

text.p: Bank of Montreal chairman Matthew Barrett said on Tuesday that he expects the bank to maintain or exceed 10 percent growth in earnings per share.

"Our outlook going forward is that we see no reason to at all to back away from our goal of producing a minimum of 10 percent earnings per share growth per year," Barrett told reporters at a news briefing after the bank released its year-end results.
The bank reported fourth quarter earnings of C$1.04 per share in the three months ended October 31, up from C$0.93 a share in the same period a year earlier.
Earnings for the full year rose to C$4.13 a share from C$3.38 a share in 1995.

The bank's net income jumped 18.4 percent to a record C$1.17 billion, the third Canadian bank to exceed C$1 billion in annual profit. "There is sufficient counter cyclicality built into the range of businesses and range of geographies that we're operating in now that we continue to feel that we would be able to maintain that 10 percent EPS growth or better in the years ahead," Barrett said.
He estimated the bank's provision for credit losses in 1997 at about C$275 million.
In 1996, Bank of Montreal lowered its provision for loan losses to C$225 million from C$275 million in 1995.
Based on its composition of assets, Barrett said the bank would normally expect loan losses to range between C$250 million and C$300 million a year.
"We will plan for next year at about C$275 (million) and we'll stick with that until we are six months into the year and see how the credit cycle shakes out," Barrett said.
